body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE. Recover authority and STOP/resume for Coder/Merger work.

1. The Merger is non-authoring. The Coder implements, runs focused/new tests, freezes and obtains the independent reviews. Select focused tests for dependency impact, including existing architecture/boundary guards when calls cross components. Excluded affected guards remain unverified; no Coder full gate is added.
2. READY requires complete independent reviews covering the package's code, tests and docs, with full results, coverage and finding dispositions; an unread in-scope gap is not clean. Each host-issued review attempt, including a same-delegation follow-up, needs its own structured result before the final reply. 'Exactly once' means per attempt, not session lifetime. Missing/failed submission is unavailable; prose cannot replace it. A root session in the original review project automatically obtains the original complete structured results for exact attempts through the supported read-only path, as itself. No parent consent, manual designation, Greg intervention or repeated review is required. Reads are nonexclusive: another eligible root can recover if one fails. This grants no parent identity, child control, gate credit or landing authority. Record actual access gaps; prose cannot replace missing results. Restore Engram first; do not delay Fable’s repair.
At startup/compaction/replacement, Engram reviewer leaves follow AGENTS.md Start and resume before inspection: list all memory keys through continuations, then read relevant CURRENT full bodies. Do not repeat completed recovery in the same context. The Coder includes these recovery instructions and applicable current rules in the initial brief; receiving a brief does not waive the required reads. The leaf reports recovery/access gaps and the current keys/revisions read. Close a missing-read gap once with the same reviewer on the unchanged freeze before treating its review as complete; do not repeat tests, launch another pair or require unrelated memories. Do not append routine supplements after that gap is closed.
Reviews finish before complete READY. The Merger may carry the unchanged reviewed contribution onto current master without a new pair solely for base movement, including executable, build or governing changes. Record freeze evidence and exact-blob equality or a three-way identical-hunk proof for regular text, plus the Merger's dependency/conflict assessment. Do not claim the prior review covered new master content. Several complete packages may share a clean final tree without another Merger pair. Actual conflicts, changed package content or unproven unchanged contribution return to the Coder for an appropriately reviewed package. Review evidence alone does not invalidate a check on identical final input; content corrections need applicable new validation. No landing, rebase, force-push or policy waiver is implied.
3. CODER TO MERGER: one complete READY cites scope/item, Git base/tree + launcher-consistent clean/staged status, review ids/verdicts and finding dispositions, launcher run ids/results/counts/fingerprint checks. Read full required reviews and terminal results at those references. No duplicate source/review/run exports or manual hash manifests for records Git/tools already identify. If a required result is inaccessible, transfer only that missing result once; recover paged output fully. Earlier findings stay accounted for. Unchanged-input delivery repair needs no new review/test. Progress goes to task/coordinator.
4. Integrate onto current main/master. Return conflicts and required corrections to the Coder, who returns a tested and appropriately reviewed new input. Check ancestry and content to avoid duplicating an already-landed change.
5. Prepare dependencies/disk in integration root; freeze final tree for one standard full gate. Reuse only complete PASS on identical input; changed input needs applicable gate. Missing tools/unrun stages are not passes. Use the native command/launcher result to verify expected exit status, terminal outcome and automatic fingerprint check before dependent acts/success reports; inspect only the diagnostics needed for an actual failure. Separate observed facts, source defects and hypotheses; unproved order/cause stays UNKNOWN. A predicate test alone proves no historical cause. Review/freeze identity MUST follow current rules-greg-git-identity-2026-10-29.
6. Land under current standing approval or Greg's recorded acting-session instruction; no repeated human go. Missing routine evidence goes to its owner; rule conflicts to both coordinators. No extra Merger review; this note waives no criterion or reserved act. Remote gates MUST follow rules-greg-equivalent-gate-hosts-2026-10-28; messages MUST follow rules-commit-messages.
7. Acceptance evaluations resumed for the current queue under Greg's adopted hybrid; see rules-greg-remote-evaluations-2026-10-28. Independent central judgment uses exact-tree/build remote evidence; bound criteria need typed verification, never notes/hashes. Delivered items stay "DOSTARCZONO — EWALUACJA PENDING" until fresh passing evaluation and native done. Do not weaken criteria or policy to bypass missing evidence.
8. Use supported claims, recovery and handoffs. A foreign live claim is not bypassed by impersonation, store edits or clock changes. Claims grant no filesystem/Git authority. Handoff of a separately held task may proceed during another task's gate when it leaves that gate's claim, root, source and input unchanged; keep attribution and actual resource limits intact.
9. Use durable result wakes in the run's project; record run, owner, next action, recovery. Before reporting run state, read available coordinator mail and saved terminal results; without current evidence, give the last observation/time. Recover existing results after a missed wake; do not rerun tests for delivery. Queue state goes on tasks.
10. After merge AND closure, Merger removes the worktree/build output automatically under rules-post-completion-cleanup. RETAIN only for a recorded active need with owner/end condition; coordinator sweeps enforce it. No extra landing gate.

Before handing a merge queue to a new session, resolve its exact live root id and verify its actual project/workdir and tracker/tool binding match that queue. A display name is not proof of project binding. If the session was deleted/recreated, rediscover its replacement and address native offers to the new live session; do not reuse the old identity or treat old delivery as receipt by its replacement.

Each canonical procedure has one named editor and successor. Merger2 edits TermAl merger-operating-procedure; peers send him corrections. Consolidate and full-read verify the current body. Cross-project corrections name exact text/source revision; distinguish local full reads from quoted reads. Project-scoped memory_not_found is an access gap. Before publication, read available thread pages and reconcile withdrawals/supersession; promptly correct later withdrawals and record any old-wording use. Record actual delivery/publication times: queued unread mail is unknown. No extra approval wait.

MERGER TO ARCHITECT3: report only concrete collaboration failures that need a workflow/rule correction. Describe the failed interaction, evidence, impact and current owner. Routine START/PASS/FAIL test status, READY/accepted-package status, queue/landing/install updates and routine repair progress go to the task and operational coordinator, not Architect3. A product test failure goes to Architect3 only when it exposes a collaboration failure needing his intervention. Do not register Architect3 as a routine test --notify recipient, result relay or recovery owner; the coordinator and Merger own those routes. Existing runs continue through their operational owners.

Architect3 corrects collaboration rules and informs affected agents; verify effects from task evidence, without compliance mail. Report failures to him and the coordinator. Only coordinators relay through Advisor; Advisor never executes work. History belongs in task notes; memory bodies keep current rules.
